prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a parking lot collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1126; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition, and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant generally denies the allegations and requests that Plaintiff be required to prove the charges and allegations against Defendant by a preponderance of the evidence.

For further answer, and without assuming any burden of proof that would otherwise rest with Plaintiff, Defendant asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's own negligence proximately caused or contributed to the occurrence in question. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by the percentage of responsibility attributed to Plaintiff, and Plaintiff is barred from recovery if that percentage exceeds fifty percent.

Second, the injuries and damages claimed were caused, in whole or in part, by a sudden emergency or by the acts or omissions of persons other than Defendant, including responsible third parties, and Defendant reserves the right to designate such persons under Section 33.004.

Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by not following reasonable medical advice or by failing to seek timely and appropriate treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this answer as discovery proceeds.
